steps.text: Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
In a medium bowl, mix together the peanut butter, sugar, egg, and baking soda until well blended. Roll dough into 1 inch balls, and place on ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake for 6 to 8 minutes in the preheated oven. Cool on cookie sheets until set, before transferring to wire racks to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick Peanut Butter Cookies
raw_recipe.description: I had to make cookies at the last minute for a school function and a friend gave me this quick and easy recipe. From start to finish, this only takes about 30-45 minutes and the taste is like you spent hours in the kitchen. You might want to make a double batch, because they will be gone before you know it. ENJOY!!
raw_recipe.name: Quick Peanut Butter Cookies

review.reviewBody: I usually use brown sugar and skip the baking soda when I make these. Be sure to let these cool on the cookie sheet for 5 minutes before removing to a wire rack, or they may fall apart.

After reading the Reviews, I just have to add my two cents. This recipe is my "Go To" when baking PBC. They're a real hit when bringing them to gatherings too. Seems like everyone is doing Gluten-Free these days. I like mine chewy rather than crunchy, so I slightly under-bake them using a parchment paper-lined baking sheet, which enables me to slide the whole sheet off to a cool surface without disturbing the cookie, then place them in an air-tight bag or container for storing. Over time, I have tweaked the recipe a bit. Vickie's recipe is delicious as is, but as my tastes have changed over time, I find that with a 1:1 ratio of sugar/peanutbutter, the end result leaves the cookie a bit too sweet for me. So, instead of the 1 cup white sugar, I substitue 1/2 cup brown sugar and 1/3 cup molasses. The molasses really intensifies the flavor and adds moistness. I also add a teaspoon of vanilla and salt omitting the baking soda.

These are a huge hit in our family. I've made them for a gluten-free friend, but we enjoy them for ourselves as well. Here are my tips: Use chunky PB (store brand is fine). Use only 1/2 cup of sugar, but use brown sugar. Cream these before adding a beaten, extra large egg. After a few seconds the batter gets very stiff. Sprinkle over the baking soda and mix it in by hand. I also add ~1/2 c. MINI CHOCOLATE CHIPS. Quickly shape the balls with a small cookie scoop, trying to pack it in well before releasing it. Place on parchment or a silicon mat. Press each ball with a fork (fixing crumbly edges if necessary). These baked up in 8-9 minutes. I don't try to move them off the cookie sheet until they are almost cool. Enjoy!

These are delicious but very fragile cookies! I doubled the recipe, added 1 cup of dark chocolate chips, 1/2 cup of chopped walnuts, 1/4th cup of rice flour, and 1/8th cup of almond meal. Several reviewers had remarked about adding rice flour to make them easier to roll. I also used half brown sugar and half regular sugar. Next time I will try using more rice flour to see if the cookies will be more sturdy. The chocolate chips and the walnuts go really well with the peanut butter! My batches took a minimum of eight minutes in the oven. I baked them in a ball on the cookie sheet and then gently used a fork to press them down slightly once they were out of the oven. I used parchment paper and let them completely cool on the cookie sheet before carefully picking them up with a fork.

Delicious! Very yummy. I substituted sugar with splenda cause hubby is diabetic n I still loved them! I added 1 tspn of vanilla n sprinkled a little sugar on top after making a criss cross pattern on the cookies. I baked them for 10 mins at 325

Based on the other suggestions, I made a couple of changes but kept the recipe gluten free. Everything the same, except 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup light brown sugar. Then added 1/4 cup coconut flour, 1/4 t. salt and 1/3 cup mini dark chocolate chips. Used a 1" cookie scoop to form the cookies, then lightly pressed with a fork to make the traditional crisis-cross design. Baked at 350 for eight min on parchment paper lined trays. Cool before transferring to a rack. Cookies were delicate with a wonderful peanut flavor. Made 28 cookies.
I'm pretty certain that the peanut butter that I used was a factor. Trader Joe's peanut butter is extremely OILY, so I added another five minutes to baking before cooling. The children loved it.

Very good and so easy to make. I added a couple extra ingredients so the dough is easier to handle and for a firmer cookie. 1/4 cup Flour & 1 tea. Vanilla and used chunky peanut butter.... Just the perfect touch! Also if you want a more cooked center bake for 10 min.

Yum! Quick pb cookie fix! Followed directions. Cooked for 8 minutes. Kept them as round balls going into the oven, as soon as they came out a added 3 chocolate chips and pushed down lightly. Had that pretty cracked look. Slight crisp outside, soft inside.

For those who are gluten free, this recipe creates tasty, peanut buttery little cookies. I add a 1/4 cup (or less) coconut flour to give it a bit more body. I also add melted chocolate to the top of each cookie. I just melt down an 88% dark cacao bar and fill in the criss cross fork marks on the top of the cookies. I also substitute the white sugar for either brown sugar or Sugar in the Raw. Everyone loves these little scrumptious cookies!!!

Doubled each ingredient, except 1 cup white sugar and 1 cup of brown sugar. Plus 1 1/2 teaspoons of vanilla. Then rolled each ball into more white sugar. Roommates and I loved them. 3 Ingredient cookies wasn't as easy to form ball nor press fork down even after refrigerating dough. Had Great Value then. 
This recipe worked great with Jiff peanut butter. 
Trying Great Value peanut butter now. We'll see.
Simple recipe takes no time to make and everybody likes them ! Maybe next time I make them add chocolate chips or coconut
Good but a bit dry .....very tasty
Better without baking soda, makes bigger but losses moisture
Followed recipe exactly. They were too sweet and crumbly.

I followed the exact recipe, but since it was practically half sugar half peanut butter, the sweetness was extreme and all I tasted was very sugary peanut butter. Later, I had a bit of the peanut butter-sugar abomination left, so I added some butter and flour (which is what you need for almost any legit cookie) and it was much better, but still pretty bad.
We love thim thank you so much yummy

I didn't add the baking soda. And not sure why you even need it. I added an extra egg and they held together perfect. Stayed super melt in your mouth good for days. Ok that's a lie. They don't last a day around my house. Love these cookies so much and that it's only 3 ingredients and your eating peanut butter cookies within 45 minutes of the craving. Makes this the perfect cookie recipe
A bit sweet for my taste, but otherwise wonderful! They were a perfect in-between of chewy and crunchy.
quick and easy to make!!!
